text:
incident-bot: Pager: billing-metrics alert triggered (severity: P2) — anomaly: usage ledger counts for PROD-us-east are ~12-18% lower than emitted tokens; delayed downstream writes observed. Auto-escalate to on-call.
ryan_oncall: ack — joining. any customer impact flagged? :thinking_face:
ada: looks like overage flags for a handful of accounts in the last 30m — CS already has one slack DM. short summary: emit timestamps lagging, aggregator lag at `usage-joiner` service.
ryan_oncall: thanks. ETA on root pipeline check? I'll grab logs from the emitter and kafka consumer.
ada: running quick query on the ledger: `SELECT count(*) FROM usage_events WHERE region='us-east' AND ts > now()-interval '1 hour';` getting ~880k vs expected ~1.03M from emitter counters.
maria_cs: we have 2 customers asking about spikes — they see delayed invoices and temporary overage flags. I'm holding comms until we know impact.
ops-jen: checking consumer group lag: `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group usage-joiner` -> `LAG 132k` on partition 3, consumer restart 12m ago. consumer logs show repeated `TimeoutException` to s3 commit.
ryan_oncall: sounds like consumer backpressure. try bumping commit timeout and restart a scaled replica. I'll trigger a single extra consumer for partition 3.
ada: started a spare consumer, lag dropped to 40k in 90s. can we pause any heavy batch backfills?
ryan_oncall: pausing backfills now (deploy pipeline job id: `deploy-7421`) — paused.
ops-jen: we see `S3 503` spikes from the region around 23:12 UTC that correlate with increased processing time. S3 retries blowing up consumer wall time.
maria_cs: which customers got overflagged? list coming.
ada: customers flagged: acct-1221, acct-3344, acct-9987; flags appear between 23:05-23:20 UTC. We'll plan to retract if counts reconcile.
ryan_oncall: mitigation checklist: 1) scale consumers (done) 2) pause backfills (done) 3) enable emitter shadow (write to shadow queue only) 4) schedule one-off ledger reconciliation job.
ada: emitter shadow enabled. starting reconcile job now: `python tools/reconcile_usage.py --from 2026-03-17T22:30Z --to 2026-03-17T23:30Z --region us-east --dry-run`
incident-bot: Note: created incident ticket INC-2026-0317-47 and paged billing-alerts channel.
maria_cs: CS: I'm drafting a hold notice. If counts fix within 2h we send a follow-up retract; otherwise prepare billing remediation plan.
ryan_oncall: quick sanity check logs from `usage-joiner`: found one stacktrace showing `NullPointer` in commit path — added a guard, pushed hotfix `joiner/patch-0.1.3` to canary.
ada: canary deployed, canary consumer healthy and acking, lag on partition 3 trending down to ~5k.
ops-jen: reconcile dry-run shows missing events ~= 138k for the window; looks like delayed writes rather than permanent loss.
ryan_oncall: good. plan: let consumers catch up, run final reconcile, then re-run billing rules to clear false overflags. target timeline 90-120m.
maria_cs: pinging customers with a brief note: "We're investigating a short-term reporting delay; your usage may show temporary overage flags that we're clearing once reconciliation completes."
ada: final reconcile job started (non-dry-run). command: ```
python tools/reconcile_usage.py --from 2026-03-17T22:30Z --to 2026-03-17T23:30Z --region us-east
```
incident-bot: Update: incident severity lowered to P3 — no active customer outages, direct billing impact under investigation.
ryan_oncall: follow-ups captured: - postmortem to include root cause (S3 transient + consumer retry plumbing), - add consumer circuit-breaker and exponential backoff caps, - add metrics for emitter->ledger end-to-end delta, - run backfill verification job nightly.
maria_cs: CS action: prepare customer impact matrix and proposed credit policy for affected accounts (acct-1221, acct-3344, acct-9987).
ops-jen: adding retry/backoff config PR: `github.com/redwood/usage-joiner#PR-512` and will coordinate canary deploy tomorrow.
ada: closing the active pager for now; will monitor logs for next 3 hours and update incident ticket.
ryan_oncall: thanks team. if anything flares I'll re-open. :thumbsup:
